title: Zaramo Wedding Feast
community: Zaramo people of the Dar es Salaam coast — the complete wedding feast
author: Chef Fatuma
desc: Zaramo Wedding Feast — the complete traditional Zaramo celebration menu. Goat pilau, coconut fish stew, cassava with greens, banana stew, forest greens, fermented drinks, and fresh tropical fruit. The feast of the original Dar es Salaam — celebrating a Zaramo wedding as it has been done for generations.
longDesc: The Zaramo wedding feast is one of Tanzania's most distinctive celebration meals — blending the coastal Swahili influences (pilau, coconut) with traditional inland Zaramo preparations (cassava, banana, forest greens). This recipe is a menu guide for assembling the complete feast.
ingredients: Goat Pilau — for the celebration rice (TZA025)
steps: Days before: prepare fermented cassava (3—4 days soaking required).
Day before: marinate goat for pilau. Prepare fermented drinks.
Morning of: begin goat pilau (longest preparation).
Midday: cook fish stew, banana stew, and forest greens.
One hour before: assemble fruit platter. Brew chai.
Serve pilau as the centrepiece. All other dishes alongside.
chefTips: The goat pilau is the most important dish — give it the most attention.
Traditional Zaramo feasts are eaten communally from shared plates.
The forest greens must be fresh — foraged or bought the same day.
commonMistakes: Not starting fermented cassava 4 days ahead.
sustainabilityTips: The Zaramo feast uses almost entirely local ingredients from the coastal ecosystem.
healthBenefits: Diverse nutritional profile from the variety of dishes.
culturalNote: The Zaramo wedding feast is a celebration of the original inhabitants of Dar es Salaam's coast — a feast that remembers what was here before the city, before the port, before the colonial era. To eat a Zaramo wedding feast is to connect with the deepest layer of the capital's history.
